segment: Mobile in-person card acceptance SDK components: Square Mobile Payments SDK (Android baseline documented at v2.7.0; documentation also covers iOS variants) and Stripe Terminal SDK (Android-specific operation guide; related platform variants only where noted). Component benchmark, not full POS products.
scope: Research only. Inventory official documented SDK/core operation behaviors relevant to merchant onboarding, permissions, payment attempt lifecycle, device/readers, offline behavior, refunds, capture/tips, receipts, privacy, and recovery. Square Android is the existing implementation starting point in OpenBMT; Stripe Terminal is an alternative component research subject only. No final provider recommendation, account access, or implementation. Platform/version/country/hardware qualifiers apply as stated per source.

claims.merchant_outcome: Install and initialize the Square Android payment component
claims.behavior: Add Square Maven dependencies and initialize MobilePaymentsSdk with developer application ID.
claims.preconditions: Android app and Square developer application ID.
claims.qualifiers: Current Android docs sample dependency version 2.7.0; SDK/API versions can change.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Wrong app ID/environment prevents successful SDK operations.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Avoid Android startup failures by validating the configured application ID/environment before showing the merchant a payment-ready state.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card SDK installation and provider credential work does not improve Bitcoin settlement; keep the card integration optional so Bitcoin acceptance can initialize and operate without provider credentials.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Separate dependency and credential boundaries reduce card-provider coupling but require the app to maintain two checkout paths and clear tender-specific recovery.
claims.acceptance_test: With a valid Android application ID and sandbox configuration, SDK initialization reaches the documented ready state; with a mismatched ID/environment, startup surfaces the initialization failure and does not offer card tender.
claims.capability: Install and initialize the Square Android payment component

claims.merchant_outcome: Authorize the SDK for a Square seller and location
claims.behavior: AuthorizationManager.authorize receives access token and location ID; production documentation says use OAuth, not a deployed personal access token.
claims.preconditions: Seller account, access token, location ID.
claims.qualifiers: Sandbox personal access token is described for tests only; production auth must use OAuth.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Handle no network/usage errors and reauthorize after expired authorization.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce seller setup retries by making the chosen seller account/location explicit and distinguishing expired authorization from network failure.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Square/Stripe seller authorization and production approval do not authorize Bitcoin; retain separate account credentials and allow the Bitcoin path when card-provider authorization is unavailable.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Provider-specific identity and permissions must stay isolated; staff may need separate setup and reconciliation steps for each tender.
claims.acceptance_test: Authorize with a valid seller token and location, then verify readiness; repeat with expired authorization and verify the documented authorization failure is surfaced with reauthorization path.
claims.capability: Authorize the SDK for a Square seller and location

claims.merchant_outcome: Request least required Square OAuth permissions
claims.behavior: Docs list MERCHANT_PROFILE_READ, PAYMENTS_WRITE, PAYMENTS_WRITE_IN_PERSON minimum; additional permissions for fees/surcharges and other APIs.
claims.preconditions: OAuth app and seller consent.
claims.qualifiers: Square OAuth token expires after 30 days; feature-specific scopes may add requirements.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Refresh token/access lifecycle must be handled; revoked/expired authorization behavior needs app handling.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce consent friction by requesting only documented payment scopes and prompting again when access expires or is revoked.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Square/Stripe seller authorization and production approval do not authorize Bitcoin; retain separate account credentials and allow the Bitcoin path when card-provider authorization is unavailable.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Provider-specific identity and permissions must stay isolated; staff may need separate setup and reconciliation steps for each tender.
claims.acceptance_test: Authorize an OAuth app with the three documented minimum scopes; verify payment works, a feature requiring an extra scope is gated, and expired access is refreshed or reauthorized.
claims.capability: Request least required Square OAuth permissions

claims.merchant_outcome: Meet Square production prerequisites
claims.behavior: Production requires enabled payment processing, app signature submission for Android SDK 2.1+, SDK initialized with production application ID, and seller authorization.
claims.preconditions: Account activation, production app credentials, application signature, reader permissions.
claims.qualifiers: Current version requirements and Square eligibility rules apply.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Sandbox success does not satisfy production approval or account/device support.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Prevent launch-day payment failures by presenting each production prerequisite as a separate setup status: account processing, signature, production app ID and seller authorization.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Square/Stripe seller authorization and production approval do not authorize Bitcoin; retain separate account credentials and allow the Bitcoin path when card-provider authorization is unavailable.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Provider-specific identity and permissions must stay isolated; staff may need separate setup and reconciliation steps for each tender.
claims.acceptance_test: Using sandbox-only setup must not be treated as production-ready; verify missing signature or disabled payment processing blocks production readiness while each completed prerequisite is recorded.
claims.capability: Meet Square production prerequisites

claims.merchant_outcome: Test virtual card flows in Square Sandbox
claims.behavior: Mock Reader UI simulates readers and payment outcomes; physical readers are not supported in Sandbox.
claims.preconditions: Sandbox app ID/account and Mock Reader dependency.
claims.qualifiers: Square Sandbox only; virtual mock reader.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Move separately to production authorization and physical-device pairing for production claims.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Shorten integration QA by exposing mock-reader status and outcome selection while clearly labeling that it does not exercise a physical reader.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Mock card reader only verifies card SDK behavior; keep Bitcoin payment tests and production readiness separate.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A card sandbox result does not validate Bitcoin invoice settlement, and vice versa; the merchant must test each path separately.
claims.acceptance_test: In Sandbox, run mock success and decline outcomes and verify results reach the app; confirm physical reader pairing is unavailable and no production compatibility claim is inferred.
claims.capability: Test virtual card flows in Square Sandbox

claims.merchant_outcome: Present Square card-entry payment UI
claims.behavior: Square default prompt offers currently available reader methods; a custom prompt is possible but app must monitor method changes.
claims.preconditions: Authorized SDK; configured PaymentParameters and PromptParameters.
claims.qualifiers: Only one payment can be in process at a time.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Unavailable entry methods or another in-flight operation should block/recover with visible state.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce cashier hesitation by presenting only the entry methods currently reported available and disabling a second attempt while one is active.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card prompts, reader inputs and pairing do not directly improve Bitcoin acceptance; preserve an independent Bitcoin tender option when the card reader is unavailable.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A shared cashier interface can reduce training, but card reader readiness must not gate Bitcoin or mislabel a Bitcoin action as a card-reader method.
claims.acceptance_test: Start one payment and verify another cannot start concurrently; detach a reader or change available methods and verify the prompt refreshes to the documented state.
claims.capability: Present Square card-entry payment UI

claims.merchant_outcome: Associate each SDK attempt with stable app references
claims.behavior: PaymentParameters include amount, paymentAttemptId and optional referenceId; SDK creates idempotency key for the attempt.
claims.preconditions: Unique attempt ID and amount.
claims.qualifiers: SDK docs describe idempotency behavior and 24-hour key retention for lookup.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: For missing server response, query payment status using referenceId/ListPayments before retrying; avoid duplicate charge.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce duplicate-charge recovery time by persisting the attempt and reference IDs with the order before handing off to card entry.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card provider idempotency and status reconciliation do not improve Bitcoin settlement directly; keep card attempt IDs separate from Bitcoin invoice/payment identifiers while preserving one merchant order reference.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A shared order record simplifies merchant reconciliation, but reusing provider idempotency keys across rails is invalid and can obscure which payment completed.
claims.acceptance_test: Start an attempt with stable paymentAttemptId/referenceId, simulate a lost response, query by reference before retry, and verify no second charge is created.
claims.capability: Associate each SDK attempt with stable app references

claims.merchant_outcome: Receive completed payment or structured payment failure
claims.trigger: Buyer presents card or chooses supported method
claims.behavior: PaymentManager callback returns Payment or PaymentError; successful Payment is accessible in Square Dashboard/Payments API.
claims.preconditions: Started payment and SDK callback lifecycle.
claims.qualifiers: SDK operation takes screen during buyer card interaction.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Application must render clear status and reconcile after lost/ambiguous callback.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Help staff distinguish approved, declined and unresolved outcomes before marking the sale paid.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card result, cancellation, consent or receipt behavior is provider-specific; maintain separate Bitcoin payment status and receipt/consent record while retaining the same merchant order.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A common order view helps staff, but provider callback and receipt semantics cannot be reused as evidence of Bitcoin settlement or receipt delivery.
claims.acceptance_test: Verify Payment callback is recorded as success; inject PaymentError and ambiguous/missing callback states and ensure neither is displayed as completed until reconciled.
claims.capability: Receive completed payment or structured payment failure

claims.merchant_outcome: Cancel or classify an in-progress payment
claims.trigger: Cashier cancels or app is interrupted
claims.behavior: PaymentHandle.cancel may return CANCELED, NO_PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS or NOT_CANCELABLE; backgrounding cancels only while still cancelable.
claims.preconditions: PaymentHandle from startPaymentActivity.
claims.qualifiers: Once sent to Square, backgrounding does not stop payment; callback still receives final result.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: NOT_CANCELABLE or uncertain outcome requires payment status reconciliation before retry.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Prevent a second charge after cancellation by showing whether cancellation succeeded, was too late, or found no active payment.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card result, cancellation, consent or receipt behavior is provider-specific; maintain separate Bitcoin payment status and receipt/consent record while retaining the same merchant order.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A common order view helps staff, but provider callback and receipt semantics cannot be reused as evidence of Bitcoin settlement or receipt delivery.
claims.acceptance_test: Cancel while payment is active and verify CANCELED; repeat after request is not cancelable and verify final callback/status is reconciled before retry.
claims.capability: Cancel or classify an in-progress payment

claims.merchant_outcome: Choose online, offline, or automatic processing path
claims.behavior: Processing mode supports ONLINE_ONLY, OFFLINE_ONLY, AUTO_DETECT; automatic selects online/offline based on conditions.
claims.preconditions: Offline payments enabled by seller and eligible setup.
claims.qualifiers: Only specified recent reader models; Sandbox offline unsupported; offline amounts/storage limits and country/device rules apply.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Offline payments queue on device and upload when process is running/connected; app termination does not schedule queued upload; monitor pending/rejected states.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce offline-payment loss by showing seller opt-in, reader eligibility, queued/pending status and upload outcome before staff closes the sale.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Bitcoin may offer a separate acceptance path when provider connectivity or offline eligibility blocks card acceptance, subject to its own network and confirmation policy.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin has separate connectivity/confirmation and reversal properties; do not represent it as equivalent to a queued card authorization or promise acceptance when its own network is unavailable.
claims.acceptance_test: For a documented eligible Square reader in offline mode, record queued status, reconnect while app remains running and verify upload result; verify unsupported Sandbox/offline configuration is blocked.
claims.capability: Choose online, offline, or automatic processing path

claims.merchant_outcome: Pair reader and show readiness, methods, and connection changes
claims.behavior: ReaderManager pairs, lists, observes statuses, and exposes reader model/methods; paired readers remembered/reconnect for authorized seller.
claims.preconditions: Production reader and required device permissions.
claims.qualifiers: Physical readers unavailable in Sandbox; reader pairing is production-only.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Handle scan timeout, unavailable/faulty/firmware states and reconnect result; do not offer non-ready methods.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce reader setup delays by exposing discovery, pairing progress and ready/faulty/unavailable status in the cashier flow.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Reader pairing/forgetting and card market eligibility are irrelevant to Bitcoin node or wallet readiness; allow those controls to fail independently.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Hardware-specific card availability does not establish Bitcoin-device or country eligibility; separate capability checks are needed.
claims.acceptance_test: Pair a supported physical reader in production, verify READY exposes its reported methods, then disconnect it and confirm checkout stops offering those methods until restored.
claims.capability: Pair reader and show readiness, methods, and connection changes

claims.merchant_outcome: Disconnect/forget an eligible paired reader
claims.behavior: readerManager.forget returns forgettable readers to unpaired state; Tap to Pay/magstripe are not forgettable.
claims.preconditions: Paired reader and SDK authorization.
claims.qualifiers: Per-device differences; forgetting a reader is not same as revoking seller OAuth access.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Check isForgettable; separately deauthorize/revoke Square OAuth integration when access should end.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce reader handoff risk by showing which devices can be forgotten and separating reader removal from seller-account access revocation.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Reader pairing/forgetting and card market eligibility are irrelevant to Bitcoin node or wallet readiness; allow those controls to fail independently.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Hardware-specific card availability does not establish Bitcoin-device or country eligibility; separate capability checks are needed.
claims.acceptance_test: Forget an eligible paired reader and verify it returns to unpaired; confirm Tap to Pay and magstripe are reported non-forgettable and OAuth revocation is a separate action.
claims.capability: Disconnect/forget an eligible paired reader

claims.merchant_outcome: Accept contactless card payments using supported Android device
claims.trigger: No reader or Tap to Pay selected
claims.behavior: Tap to Pay Android uses same payment flow; ReaderManager reports device capability and available contactless method.
claims.preconditions: Compatible device, enabled feature, current SDK, authorization and location.
claims.qualifiers: Country/device eligibility varies; paired Square reader may need to be forgotten/disconnected to display Tap to Pay prompt.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Check READY and available card-entry methods before offering; device/account failures need an alternate tender.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Avoid presenting Tap to Pay where device, country or reader state is unverified; show eligibility as unknown until checked for the actual deployment.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card prompts, reader inputs and pairing do not directly improve Bitcoin acceptance; preserve an independent Bitcoin tender option when the card reader is unavailable.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A shared cashier interface can reduce training, but card reader readiness must not gate Bitcoin or mislabel a Bitcoin action as a card-reader method.
claims.acceptance_test: On a documented eligible device/region, verify Tap to Pay appears only when capability is ready; with paired reader state that suppresses the prompt, show the documented disconnect/forget path.
claims.capability: Accept contactless card payments using supported Android device

claims.merchant_outcome: Resolve declined or lost-response outcomes without duplicate charges
claims.behavior: Re-use payment attempt ID lookup/idempotency key and query ListPayments by referenceId/fields to determine existing status before another attempt.
claims.preconditions: Stored stable reference/attempt ID.
claims.qualifiers: Square docs state idempotency key retention and fallback if key unavailable.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Unknown remains unresolved until ListPayments/status reconciliation; retry may need a new attempt after known prior incomplete payment.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce duplicate recovery attempts by making unknown status a hold state and showing the reconciliation result tied to the original reference.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card provider idempotency and status reconciliation do not improve Bitcoin settlement directly; keep card attempt IDs separate from Bitcoin invoice/payment identifiers while preserving one merchant order reference.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A shared order record simplifies merchant reconciliation, but reusing provider idempotency keys across rails is invalid and can obscure which payment completed.
claims.acceptance_test: Create a timeout with known referenceId; query ListPayments; if existing payment appears, reconcile it instead of retrying; if absent, follow documented new-attempt flow.
claims.capability: Resolve declined or lost-response outcomes without duplicate charges

claims.merchant_outcome: Refund eligible payment through Square Refunds API
claims.behavior: Refunds API can refund SDK-created payment; creates separate refund operation and object.
claims.preconditions: Payment ID, refund API integration and permissions.
claims.qualifiers: Refund is not a Mobile Payments SDK action; API availability/limits vary by transaction/provider policy.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Track pending/failure and reconcile Refund object; do not equate local request with paid refund.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce refund follow-up by showing the Square refund request separately from the final refund object/status.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card capture/refund lifecycle does not apply to Bitcoin settlement; keep a Bitcoin refund/return workflow explicit and allow card operations to remain provider-controlled.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin refunds may require a separate outbound transfer and fee/approval flow; merchant must not assume card-style reversal or provider refund state.
claims.acceptance_test: Submit refund API request for an eligible SDK-created payment and verify refund object/status is persisted; a pending or failed response must not be shown as completed refund.
claims.capability: Refund eligible payment through Square Refunds API

claims.merchant_outcome: Delay payment capture for eligible checkout workflow
claims.trigger: Order fulfillment or receipt tip requires delayed completion
claims.behavior: Set autocomplete false to authorize then later complete or cancel; delayAction can cancel or complete after configured duration.
claims.preconditions: PaymentParameters support delayed capture and server/API update where applicable.
claims.qualifiers: Duration default/maximum and transaction type constraints apply; not general long-lived authorization.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Capture/complete status can be reconciled; stale uncaptured authorization may expire.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce uncaptured-payment loss by showing authorization age, capture deadline and explicit complete/cancel actions to the operator.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card capture/refund lifecycle does not apply to Bitcoin settlement; keep a Bitcoin refund/return workflow explicit and allow card operations to remain provider-controlled.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Bitcoin refunds may require a separate outbound transfer and fee/approval flow; merchant must not assume card-style reversal or provider refund state.
claims.acceptance_test: Create eligible delayed-capture payment, complete before documented expiry and verify completed state; separately cancel and verify order does not remain marked paid.
claims.capability: Delay payment capture for eligible checkout workflow

claims.merchant_outcome: Add tip through app-owned UI and supported payment update
claims.trigger: Buyer chooses tip before or after authorization
claims.behavior: SDK has no built-in tipping UI; app builds UI and may set tip parameter/update eligible payment prior to completion.
claims.preconditions: Payment flow and Payments API where needed.
claims.qualifiers: Relevant payment state and delayed-capture conditions apply.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Reconcile final total and show tip distinctly on receipt.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce tip-entry errors by keeping tip amount distinct from base amount and reflecting the final supported amount before completion.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card tip update is not a Bitcoin tip workflow; preserve a tender-independent gratuity field only if merchant requirements and Bitcoin accounting can support it.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Tip changes can alter the amount after initial authorization; Bitcoin payments may require a new invoice/settlement rather than a card-style update.
claims.acceptance_test: Enter tip through app UI on eligible flow; verify final payment amount includes configured tip and receipt shows tip separately; reject updates after unsupported state.
claims.capability: Add tip through app-owned UI and supported payment update

claims.merchant_outcome: Provide buyer printed or digital receipt option
claims.behavior: Square requires app to offer receipt option; app generates required fields from payment response or may use receipt URL when available.
claims.preconditions: Completed payment result and app receipt workflow.
claims.qualifiers: Square does not directly send receipts; receipt URL only on completed payments.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Handle not-yet-completed/failed payment distinctly and do not claim receipt issued until delivery confirmed.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce missing receipts by treating receipt selection, generation and delivery as distinct states after payment completion.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card result, cancellation, consent or receipt behavior is provider-specific; maintain separate Bitcoin payment status and receipt/consent record while retaining the same merchant order.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A common order view helps staff, but provider callback and receipt semantics cannot be reused as evidence of Bitcoin settlement or receipt delivery.
claims.acceptance_test: Complete payment and offer documented receipt choices; verify only completed payment can use receipt URL and failed/incomplete payments cannot be labeled receipted.
claims.capability: Provide buyer printed or digital receipt option

claims.merchant_outcome: Collect required data privacy consent when using custom prompt
claims.behavior: Default Square prompt collects privacy consent; custom prompt implementer must collect consent and call settingsManager.updateTrackingConsent.
claims.preconditions: Custom PromptMode and relevant regional requirements.
claims.qualifiers: Consent requirements vary by region.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Payment start can fail with CONSENT_NOT_PROVIDED; recover by capturing seller choice before starting.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Reduce consent omissions by using the default prompt where appropriate or blocking custom-prompt payment start until seller privacy choice is recorded.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Card result, cancellation, consent or receipt behavior is provider-specific; maintain separate Bitcoin payment status and receipt/consent record while retaining the same merchant order.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: A common order view helps staff, but provider callback and receipt semantics cannot be reused as evidence of Bitcoin settlement or receipt delivery.
claims.acceptance_test: Use custom prompt without consent and verify CONSENT_NOT_PROVIDED; record consent through documented settings update and verify attempt can proceed.
claims.capability: Collect required data privacy consent when using custom prompt

claims.merchant_outcome: Present available card methods based on reader attachment
claims.behavior: Reader type determines swipe/contactless/chip entry; custom UI listens for available method changes.
claims.preconditions: Supported Square reader/device pairing.

limitations: Documentation only; no vendor accounts, live reader sessions, physical device checks, or merchant tests were performed.
Square Android docs currently show Mobile Payments SDK 2.7.0; document behavior and APIs can change, and iOS has distinct platform instructions.
Square Sandbox uses virtual/mock readers and does not establish physical reader or production eligibility.
Stripe Terminal capabilities vary by platform, reader model, country, account, currency and configuration; general Android documentation is not a device certification.
Unlisted hardware, country, account, or peripheral behavior is unknown unless the specific official source explicitly states a restriction.

Square/Stripe components represent card authorization/settlement rails. They do not establish Bitcoin receipt, custody, conversion, or authority behavior. Bitcoin must remain an independently supported tender in any OpenBMT integration.

Stripe Billing, Connect, Banking, Payment Element/web checkout and other adjacent products are excluded. Square unrelated web/in-app payment products are excluded except Payments/Refund APIs explicitly used to complete SDK lifecycle behavior.
